## Catalog requirements

15 credits are required for the minor:
Course | Title | Credits
Korean Language and Language-Related Courses
Select two courses devoted specifically to Korean language or language-related studies from the following: 1 | 6
KORA201 | Intermediate Korean I
KORA202 | Intermediate Korean II
KORA211
KORA212
KORA241 | History of the Korean Language
KORA242
KORA311
KORA312
KORA345
Korea-Related Courses
Select three courses in Korea-related studies from fields such as history, sociology, and art history: 2 | 9
HIST319 | Special Topics in History (HIST319N Korean History)
SOCY398 | Special Topics in Sociology (SOCY398K Contemporary South Korean Society )
HIST284 | East Asian Civilization I 3
HIST285 | East Asian Civilization II 3
HIST319 | Special Topics in History (HIST319C Asian Age in World History )
EALL300 | The Languages of East Asia 2
GVPT359 | Topics in Comparative Politics (GVPT359C Politics of Japan and Northeast Asia )
ARTH290 | Art and Society in Asia 3
Total Credits | 15
1
Both must be at the second-year level or above.
Both must be at the second-year level or above.
2
At least one of these courses must have broad East Asian content to provide breadth to the minor.
At least one of these courses must have broad East Asian content to provide breadth to the minor.
3
East Asian courses
East Asian courses
Other Korea-related courses may be used to satisfy the requirements, subject to the approval of the Korean Program advisor.
Three of the five required courses must be at the 3xx or 4xx level.
All courses presented for the minor must be passed with a grade of "C-" or better.
An overall GPA of 2.0 in the minor is required for graduation.
No more than six credits can overlap with the major, and no more than six credits can come from off-campus (study abroad, transfer, etc.).
Note: CIC courses through the Big10 courseshare arrangements will be considered for the Korean Studies Minor

The Korean Language Program offers a minor for undergraduates. Our language program is a 2-year sequence of skills courses, to include speaking, reading, writing, and culture, with expansion to third-year Korean a future possibility. Before registering, students new to the program need to take the college’s online World Language Placement Assessment (WLP). The Korean Studies minor combines Korean Program courses with Korea-related courses offered by departments across campus.

Undergraduate Studies
Minors are an excellent way for students to gain expertise in an area beyond the major. We encourage students to work with their advisors early to incorporate the minor into their Academic Plans.
Applications for all minors remain open until the minor is filled. Students will be taken on a first-come, first-served basis. When you click on the “contact form” below and select the appropriate option on the form, your request will be marked with the date and time. Please keep in mind that any pre-requisites must be completed by the time of application. (Students applying to the Music Performance minor must successfully pass an audition and should contact the advisor through the form below as soon as possible.)
When a minor is listed as CLOSED, it is closed until October 1 in the fall semester or March 1 in the spring semester. You may check this site again at these times. When a minor is listed as WAITLIST, it is closed, but you may put yourself on a waitlist by clicking on "contact form" below and selecting the appropriate option.
